question.text: Ranjit invested USD 10,000 in a US equity fund when the exchange rate was INR 75/USD. After one year, the fund earned 12% in USD terms, but the INR appreciated to INR 72/USD. What is Ranjit's approximate return in INR terms?

explanation.text: The Logic: Initial investment in INR = 10,000 x 75 = Rs. 7,50,000. USD value after 1 year = 10,000 x 1.12 = USD 11,200. INR value at new rate = 11,200 x 72 = Rs. 8,06,400. INR return = (8,06,400 - 7,50,000)/7,50,000 = 56,400/7,50,000 = 7.52%. The Trap: 12.00% ignores the currency impact entirely. 16.00% incorrectly adds the fund return and a currency gain (as if INR had depreciated). 9.00% applies an approximate currency adjustment without compounding correctly. INR appreciation reduces the rupee return from foreign-currency investments. Note: Distributor/cross-exam framing removed; only the source-grounded INR-return calculation retained.
